title: Hierarchical runtime operator fallback and calibration safety-net for mixed-precision dispatch
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a hierarchical decision layer in the runtime dispatcher that selects between FP16, FP8, and INT8 operator kernels using pre-computed quantization profiles, online calibration confidence, and workload telemetry; provide robust safety-net fallbacks and a validation pipeline so we can safely enable mixed-precision paths in hosted and dedicated deployments.

Scope:
- Decision/dispatch logic in the serving process that evaluates: model quant profile metadata, per-layer calibration statistics, token sequence length, KV cache hit patterns, and latency SLO targets.
- Integrate calibration artifacts: per-layer scale/zero-point metadata for INT8, FP8 exponent biases where applicable, and a compact confidence score from the calibration runner.
- Implement three fallback tiers: (1) within-kernel precision fallback (e.g., FP8->FP16 within same operator when error estimate high), (2) per-layer operator replacement to higher-precision variant, and (3) route entire request to safe FP16 path if cumulative error exceeds threshold.
- Hook the dispatcher into the calibration workflow so newly uploaded quant profiles can be validated and assigned a dispatch policy (aggressive, conservative, gated) and an experimental tag for canary rollouts.
- Telemetry: emit per-request decision traces (chosen precision per-layer, confidence scores, token latency, and quality signals) to enable offline accuracy regressions and automated rollback triggers.

Why this work: Existing quant-based dispatchers choose kernels by static profile only; that leaves us exposed to distribution shift (longer sequences, high-variance attention patterns, or emergent tokens) causing occasional accuracy regressions. A hierarchical, confidence-aware fallback reduces customer-visible regressions while preserving cost/latency gains of lower-precision paths.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime provides deterministic dispatch path decision given a quant profile and request metadata
Safety-net fallbacks trigger and route to FP16 for >95% of simulated high-error calibration cases in unit harness
A/B canary comparing mixed-precision policy vs FP16 shows no statistically significant degradation on held-out eval (delta perplexity < 0.5%) and task metrics within configured thresholds
Telemetry events include chosen-precision-per-layer, calibration-confidence, latency-per-token, and a decision-reason code
Rollout controls exist in Console to mark a policy: experimental, gradual, or forced-rollback
E2E smoke tests for hosted and Dedicated run in CI and pass under both simulated low-latency and high-latency conditions
updates: 2025-11-03: Ticket created. Initial design sketch in doc: /docs/quant/hierarchical-dispatch-design-v1.md. Assigned to Diego.

2025-11-06: Spike complete: measured per-layer calibration variance on gpt-medium-family on 1000-sample eval. Observed layer-7 attention heads show large INT8 quantization bias at long sequences. Added 'layer-sensitivity' score to decision inputs.

2025-11-09: Design review with PM (Hannah Chen) and Runtime leads. Decision: use 3-tier fallback and include a fast single-token confidence recomputation path for streaming requests. Action: add telem fields and light-weight confidence estimator.

2025-11-12: Prototype implemented: dispatcher selects kernels using (profile.priority_hint, layer-sensitivity, runtime-confidence). Built operator-level FP8->FP16 fallback. Benchmarks: latency overhead +2.5% median, cost saving ~18% on mixed-precision traces.

2025-11-16: Engineering review feedback: requestID-level trace volume concerns. Agreement to emit sampled detailed traces (1% default) and aggregate counters at full rate. Add dashboard for per-policy regression detection.

2025-11-18: Integration test fail: Canary showed a 0.9% perplexity increase on a conversational eval when sequence length >1024. Root cause: FP8 bias under rare token combos in particular embeddings layer. Mitigation: add conservative gating for embedding and first transformer block; update fallback threshold for long sequences.

2025-11-20: Updated decision graph and calibration ingestion pipeline. Prepared PRs: GH#redwood/runtime PR 8423 (dispatcher logic) and PR 8429 (telemetry schema). Ready for small canary rollout behind feature flag.
